summary: Yoshito S. Hakeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served at Columbia University as a Professor in 1966 and until 1983 as an Associate Professor in Japanese and Religion.
Yoshitoyo Ohara worked in the fields of history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Ohara held posts attested at Kyoto University in 2006 and at Kyoto National Museum in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tohoku and Harvard universities under scholars including John B. Carman, and served as a professor and Dean of the Faculty of Humanities at Tenri University from around 1984 to 2017.

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yonezawa held positions at Taisho University attested between 1998 and 2026, and was affiliated with the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies as a visiting researcher in 2026.

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe works in computational fields and Tibetology. He earned a doctorate in science from Tohoku University (1972–1975) and served there as a Senior Research Fellow (1975–2012, 2018), alongside visiting and concurrent professorships in Japan, the US, and China.

Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1939. He served as a Professor at Rissho University from around 1968 to 1987 and as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Yosuke Fujimoto works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Fujimoto studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a Research Fellow post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies from 2025 to 2026.

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held positions at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang was a philosopher and sinologist. In 1890, he founded the Wanmu Caotang academy, where he taught and held a post from approximately 1891 to 1898.

Yozo Taniyama works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and later held an appointment there around 2012 in the Department of Practical Religious Studies, along with posts at Shitennoji, St. Thomas, and Sophia universities.

Yrjö Moses Jalmari Biese was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Helsinki under J. N. Reuter, later serving there as a docent and acting professor, and as Professor of English at the University of Turku (1946–1967).

Yu Liu works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Liu earned degrees from Beijing Normal University-Hong Kong Baptist University UIC, HKBU, and the University of Hong Kong, later working as a research assistant at UIC and an editor at HK Ta Kung Wen Wei Media Group.
Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Tsui pursued master's studies at Columbia University supervised by Chün-fang Yü, completed doctoral research under Natasha Heller, and studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-Yin Hsu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Hsu completed a Ph.D. at the National University of Singapore between 2014 and 2019 and held a post in the Faculty of East Asian Studies at Ruhr University Bochum in 2022.

Yu-kwan Ng is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and earned a Ph.D. at McMaster University. Ng held academic posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~2002–2011).
Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and art history scholar who studied under John C. Huntington. Lee served as a Professor at National Taiwan University, attested in 2002.
Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff, attested in 1998.

Yuanxing Guo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism as a researcher and at the Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under masters including Tongzhi and Miaolian. He served as abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples, founded Yuanming Lengyan School, and was the first president of the Buddhist Association of China.
